cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Fake the Expertise
cards.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I'll get your boiler running. I know these controls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've been adjusting the kitchen timer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Establishing the heating interval. Call the engineer; I'll need someone on the boiler.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He asks what temperature you measured.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him we're still establishing the baseline. Put him on speaker; I'll ask the questions so he can concentrate on readings.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 vague teaching claim precedes boiler confidence; A3 nearly-my-way does not explain B2 correct identification; A5 controls engineer without maintaining pupil relation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 timer correction yields A3 interval claim; B4 measured-temperature query yields A5 baseline evasion and control.

relationship.evidence: B4 relays a plausible diagnostic question from the contacted engineer.

heightening.evidence: A5 keeps expertise performance by directing the actual expert rather than supplying nonexistent measurement.

specificity.evidence: A1 boiler and B2 kitchen timer expose the competence gap clearly.
